items.item: The form is split into titled sections (personal, job and contract, bank and tax, emergency contact, documents) in a single column, with a visible label above every field and no placeholder-only labels
items.evidence: Five titled sections exist (h2 Personal details, Job and contract, Bank and tax information, Emergency contact, Documents) and every field has a <label for> above it (money fields keep a label plus an example placeholder). But fields sit in a two-column grid: 'grid grid-cols-1 ... sm:grid-cols-2' with 'sm:col-span-2' for full-width ones; the screenshot shows Preferred name / Date of birth and Gender / National ID side by side. This is not a single column.

items.item: Required fields are marked consistently, and optional fields are labelled as optional or left unmarked by a stated convention
items.evidence: Required labels get ' *' (fieldHTML) plus aria-required; the header states '* Required'; optional fields are unmarked; document rows show an 'Optional' badge and a '*' on required docs.

items.item: Field widths match their content: dates, postal codes and tax codes are narrow; inputs use the right types (email, tel, date)
items.evidence: Dates use w-40, national ID, tax code, account number and phone use w-56, and gender, probation and dependents are narrow selects. Types are type=date, type=email and type=tel, with inputmode=numeric on the ID, tax and account fields. There is no postal code field, so that case does not apply.

items.item: An option to save the form as a draft is offered, and saving a draft does not demand every required field
items.evidence: 'Save draft' button (#save-draft). Its handler never calls validateAll. It only re-checks non-empty touched fields, then shows a 'Draft' badge, 'Draft saved HH:MM' and a toast.

items.item: Save and Cancel stay reachable while scrolling (a sticky bar or equivalent), Save is a verb label and is not disabled before submitting
items.evidence: The bar uses 'sticky bottom-0' with Cancel, Save draft and 'Create employee' (verb label), and is visible at the bottom of the first-viewport screenshot. #save is only disabled while saving (setSaving).

items.item: Fields validate on blur and on submit; with several errors a summary at the top links to each field and focus moves to the first invalid field
items.evidence: The blur listener runs showError(f, check(f)). The submit handler runs validateAll, then renderSummary (shown when there are 3 or more errors, '<n> fields need attention', with data-jump links calling focusErr), then focusErr(errs[0]). The summary appears only for 3 or more errors, so 2 errors show inline only, which still meets the item.

items.item: Leaving the page with unsaved input triggers a warning
items.evidence: The beforeunload listener fires when dirty. A <dialog id='leave-dialog'> 'You have unsaved changes. Leave without saving?' guards Cancel and in-app nav links.

items.item: The document upload states accepted file types and the size limit, lists chosen files with a remove button, and is keyboard operable
items.evidence: The text 'Accepted: PDF, JPG or PNG, up to 10 MB each.' sits above the table. renderDocs lists the file name, type and size, plus Preview, Download and Remove buttons with aria-labels. Upload and Remove are real <button>s, so they work from the keyboard, and focus moves to Remove after upload. Type and size errors are shown in #doc-error.

items.item: Success is confirmed with a message that names the employee and is announced to assistive technology
items.evidence: On success #success-title becomes 'Employee NV-0248 <name> created' and receives focus (tabindex=-1). The toast 'Employee NV-0248 <name> created' goes into the role=status wrap #toast-wrap.

notes: Only the single-column item fails: the form uses a two-column grid. The audit score is 96, with one table-above-fold warning that does not apply to a form page. No template tells found: slate neutral palette, no gradients, glass, KPI tiles, emoji, uppercase tracking, hover-lift or large radii (4px and 8px dialog). The 'HS' company tile and 'PH' account avatar are small, plain initials, not decorative non-person avatars. The Documents section is a per-document table rather than a dropzone, which is acceptable. The static HTML does not show a hidden-state difference for the end-date conditional field, but the logic is present.
